beats.text: Most AI search systems query once at the prompt, then confidently hallucinate for three paragraphs.
beats.visual_focus: Split view: prompt initiates a single database lookup, followed by a runaway red text drift

beats.text: Single-shot RAG is like checking a map once before a cross-country drive. Ten miles in, road conditions change and your model crashes into fiction.
beats.visual_focus: Car speeding down an evolving highway relying on an outdated snapshot map, crashing into a warning barrier

beats.text: FLARE replaces static retrieval with active anticipation. Instead of looking backward, the model continuously tracks its own uncertainty as text unfolds.
beats.visual_focus: Forward radar beam projecting from the current sentence position into future token space

beats.text: It speculatively drafts the upcoming sentence. If token confidence drops below threshold, that draft becomes a search query, pulling documents to regenerate verified facts.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook got me immediately because anyone who has built a basic RAG pipeline knows that exact pain—it fetches once at the prompt and then completely drifts off into hallucination land three paragraphs later. Beat 4 explains the actual mechanism brilliantly: drafting the sentence ahead, watching token confidence drop, and turning that weak draft into the next search query. That's real engineering logic, not dumbed-down fluff.
